Rachel — thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is a rough demand profile (xlsx): expected 99th p99 latency target is 120ms for our chat endpoint, 95th p95 for embeddings 60ms. Peak concurrent sessions estimated at ~420 (concurrent active chats) during our US evening hours, average session length 60s, median seq len 512 tokens, 1.2B gen tokens/month.

We plan to run two model families: a 70B encoder-decoder for contextual chat (large KV and memory pressure) and a smaller 7B for high-concurrency low-cost fallbacks. Budget guidance from procurement: prefer reserved capacity commitment for baseline, but allow 2-3x burst maximum during launch.

Victor — thanks, got the file. Looping in Dev (runtime) and Marissa (dedicated sales) to propose a concrete fleet coverage plan. High level notes before we prep a slide deck:

- Two model families imply mixed requirements: the 70B encoder-decoder is memory-bound (large KV caches, longer context) and benefits most from H100-class memory and NVLink topology; the 7B fallback is latency/batch sensitive and can be very cost-efficient on L4 with FP16/4-bit quantization.
- Recommendation pattern: reserved baseline to cover steady-state 95% of expected QPS; burst pool (on-demand or reserved burst credits) to absorb launch spikes up to 2.5-3x. This minimizes committed cost while preserving SLOs.
- Initial conservative split (12mo plan): reserve ~48% of average sustained capacity on H100 for the 70B family, reserve L4 capacity for ~70% of the frequent low-latency requests, and keep A100 as a flexible mid-point for warm fallover and A/B testing.

Action: Dev and I will produce a concrete SKU-level table (counts, vGPU equivalence, expected throughput) and two cost scenarios (conservative vs aggressive). Expect deliverable by EOD Wed.

Thanks — rachel

Victor / Alex — attaching the SKU-level tradeoffs and a sample compute plan (pdf + short MP). TL;DR summary below — full numbers are in the tables/attachment.

Summary recommendations (based on your demand profile):

1) Baseline reserved: 6x H100 (80GB) + 10x L4 
   - H100s handle the 70B models with large KV cache, support longer contexts (4k+), and deliver predictable p95/p99 for complex generations. We estimate one H100 can sustain ~28 concurrent 70B sessions (mixed sequence lengths, batching tuned) at p95 ~140ms; reserve 6 gives headroom plus some autoscale for small bursts.
   - L4s are cost-effective for 7B fallback. One L4 supports ~120 concurrent small sessions at p95 ~40-60ms depending on batching; reserve 10 to cover most daytime volume.

2) Burst pool (on-demand or short-term reserved credits): 12x L4 + 3x A100 (40GB)
   - L4 burst covers massive concurrency surges (cheap per-token). A100s are used as a warm mid-tier for workload spikes where memory/perf tradeoff sits between H100 and L4 (e.g., 20B experiments or when quantization impacts quality).

3) Autoscaling policy: keep per-model KV cache warm on H100s for top 20% of traffic to reduce cold-start latency; use prefix-caching for repeated prompts. Configure pre-warm thresholds at 2x sustained surge detection within 10 minutes.

4) Cost/throughput ballpark: conservative committed monthly cost estimate (region US) with above mix: ~$210k/month reserved + variable burst usage estimated $45-90k/month at typical launch cadence. Per-token delivered cost depends on batching efficiency; expect $0.0009-$0.0022 per generated token across mixed traffic (lower when L4 dominates).

Open questions for Vectra:
- Can you confirm percent of traffic that requires 70B-level contextual accuracy vs acceptable fallbacks? (Victor: you mentioned ~35% but wanted validated).
- Any regulatory constraints that require on-prem or dedicated single-tenant racks in month 1?

I attached: fleet_tradeoff_v2.pdf (SKU tables + throughput matrix) and a short mutual_action_plan_vectra.docx that maps next steps and procurement milestones.

-Dev
